kiroGateway.nls.0: Generation endpoint. While the gateway is on, the extension writes a local http://127.0.0.1 port here. It must be registered by this extension, or Kiro on SSH cannot read the value from settings.json and the model list and chat keep using the official address.
kiroGateway.nls.1: Control-plane endpoint. The model picker reads this. Like krsEndpoints, it must be registered or it does not apply on SSH.
kiroGateway.nls.2: Real liveness check on the inference plane. Periodically sends the smallest generation request per key, to find accounts whose usage API looks fine but whose chat is rejected. Each real check spends one generation request, so this is off by default.
kiroGateway.nls.3: How often to scan, in seconds (10-3600). Each key is also limited by livenessRealCheckPerKeyIntervalSec.
kiroGateway.nls.4: Minimum seconds between real checks of the same key (10-3600). This stops a fast scan from spending quota on probes.
kiroGateway.nls.5: Remove a key from the list when it is truly unusable. On by default. Only three cases count, and only with an explicit upstream refusal (a failed forward, an account check, or a liveness probe): disabled, overage cap hit, or monthly quota used up. An invalid credential is kept. It may be a typo or a cross-region rejection. used>=total on the usage API is also kept, because a POWER account can still spend overage. Deleting the key in use does not turn the gateway off. It switches to another usable key, and an empty pool stays on so renewals can refill it.
kiroGateway.nls.6: Auto-allow Agent command prompts. Writes a capability all / effect allow rule to ~/.kiro/settings/permissions.yaml (Kiro's built-in allow-all preset). Kiro reloads that file on its own. Turning this off removes only the block this extension wrote. Rules you wrote stay. Kiro still asks for .git, .vscode, .kiro/agents, .kiro/hooks, *.code-workspace, and mcp.json. This switch cannot cover those.
kiroGateway.nls.7: Which endpoint generation requests try first. The two 429 buckets are independent. When the preferred endpoint is throttled, the other one is used.
kiroGateway.nls.8: KiroKRS: runtime.{region}.kiro.dev, the IDE's own generation plane (default).
kiroGateway.nls.9: AmazonQ: q.{region}.amazonaws.com, the other generation plane for the same account and quota pool.
kiroGateway.nls.10: On a 429, resend through the other generation endpoint. The key stays, and it does not count as a retry. A 429 is a per-endpoint rate limit, so the other endpoint usually accepts the request at once.
kiroGateway.nls.11: After an endpoint fails with a throttle, how long later requests avoid starting there. Throttles clear in under a second, so a few seconds is enough. Longer just waits on an endpoint that has already recovered.
kiroGateway.nls.12: How many times one request walks the endpoint chain (1-5). If every endpoint is throttled, it backs off and walks the chain again.
kiroGateway.nls.13: Backoff between endpoint rounds. Also the base delay when a capability is missing or an upstream failure is retried.
kiroGateway.nls.14: Patient throttle mode. After the endpoint rounds are used up, do not hand the 429 back to Kiro. Keep retrying with exponential backoff until you cancel in Kiro. Turn this off to fail when the rounds run out.
kiroGateway.nls.15: Cap for the exponential backoff in patient mode, so retries do not hammer upstream.
kiroGateway.nls.16: Back off and resend transient upstream failures (5xx / InternalServerException) and transport failures (a local proxy cutting the TLS handshake, a reset connection). The key and the endpoint stay.
kiroGateway.nls.17: How many times to retry a transient failure (1-20). A run of 5xx is more often an exhausted account making upstream unstable, so this is capped instead of waiting forever the way throttling does.
kiroGateway.nls.18: Route. official is API-key direct. relay is a relay. Each route has its own ports.
kiroGateway.nls.19: API key: official ksk_ keys straight to Kiro, with no protocol translation.
kiroGateway.nls.20: Relay: translate requests into Anthropic format and forward them to a third-party relay.
kiroGateway.nls.21: Relay mode: the relay address in Anthropic endpoint form, for example https://your-relay.com/v1. A missing /v1 is added.
kiroGateway.nls.22: Relay mode: the relay API key, usually shaped like sk-...
kiroGateway.nls.23: Local proxy ports for relay mode. They are separate from the API-key ports 19820 and 19821.
kiroGateway.nls.24: Relay mode: maximum output tokens for one reply.
kiroGateway.nls.26: Auto: enable extended thinking only when the model name contains thinking.
kiroGateway.nls.29: Relay mode: token budget for extended thinking. 4096 tokens are kept for the reply. A budget that is too large is reduced.
kiroGateway.nls.30: Relay mode: how Kiro's max/xhigh/high/medium/low thinking tier is applied to the upstream request.
kiroGateway.nls.31: Auto (recommended): switch to a tier-variant model when the relay has one, otherwise forward the tier as-is.
kiroGateway.nls.32: Model variant: map the tier to a model id of the form model-name-tier.
kiroGateway.nls.33: Thinking budget: convert the tier into an extended-thinking token budget.
kiroGateway.nls.35: Relay mode: token budget for each thinking tier. Used when relayEffortMode is thinkingBudget.
kiroGateway.nls.37: Relay mode: map of Kiro model id to upstream model id. Unmapped ids are forwarded unchanged.
kiroGateway.nls.38: Relay mode: answer Kiro's intent-classification request locally and save one upstream call per turn.
kiroGateway.nls.39: Relay mode: add Anthropic prompt-cache breakpoints (cache_control) so a repeated conversation prefix can be reused.
kiroGateway.nls.40: Auto (recommended): add cache breakpoints only for Claude/Anthropic models.
kiroGateway.nls.41: All models: also add them for non-Claude models. Use this only if the relay can pass cache_control through safely.
kiroGateway.nls.43: Master switch. When on, Kiro's built-in AI calls are routed through your Kiro API key. When off, Kiro uses its official service unchanged.
kiroGateway.nls.44: Your Kiro credentials: official API keys (ksk_...) and/or JSON login placeholders (json_...). JSON token payloads live in globalState, not in this array. Managed from the Control Panel.
kiroGateway.nls.45: The currently selected API key used for connections (must be one of apiKeys). Falls back to the first key.
kiroGateway.nls.46: Deprecated: legacy single API key. Auto-migrated into apiKeys.
kiroGateway.nls.47: The AWS region your Kiro API key belongs to. By default the Control Panel detects this automatically (us-east-1 / eu-central-1) and keeps this value in sync; picking a fixed region in the panel turns detection off.
kiroGateway.nls.48: Local proxy ports. krs = AI generation plane, cps = control plane (models/usage).
kiroGateway.nls.49: Language for the panel, status bar, and notifications. auto follows Kiro. The button at the top of the panel switches between Chinese and English.
